title: Point, Contextual & Collective Anomalies
interviewAnswer: Anomalies can be unusual individual points, unusual only in context, or unusual sequences/groups. The detection method should match the anomaly definition rather than treating every extreme value as the same problem.
keyPoints: Context can be time, user, device or season.
why: Point, Contextual & Collective Anomalies appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Context can be time, user, device or season.
deepDive: Anomalies can be unusual individual points, unusual only in context, or unusual sequences/groups. The detection method should match the anomaly definition rather than treating every extreme value as the same problem. Collective anomalies require sequence/group features. Anomaly labels are often scarce. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A temperature of 30°C may be normal in summer but anomalous in winter for the same sensor.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

How would you validate or debug Point, Contextual & Collective Anomalies in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
